column1: environment|The natural world and the conditions around us.|The new waste scheme should benefit the local environment.
pollution|Harmful substances or effects introduced into the environment.|Residents are concerned about pollution from heavy traffic.
emission|Gas or another substance released into the environment.|The transport plan aims to reduce vehicle emissions.
climate|The usual weather conditions of a region over time.|The changing climate may affect local water supplies.
climate change|Long-term changes in weather patterns and temperatures.|The council is preparing for the effects of climate change.
sustainable|Able to continue without exhausting resources or causing lasting harm.|The town needs a more sustainable transport system.
renewable|Naturally replaced so that it can be used again.|The project will supply electricity from renewable sources.
energy|Power used for heating, lighting or operating equipment.|Better insulation can reduce household energy use.
conservation|Careful protection and management of natural resources.|The community group supports the conservation of local wetlands.
preserve|To protect something from damage or loss.|The plan aims to preserve access to the historic gardens.
protect|To keep someone or something safe from harm.|New barriers will protect pedestrians from passing traffic.
reduce|To make something smaller in amount or extent.|The council wants to reduce waste sent to landfill.
reuse|To use something again rather than throw it away.|The repair café encourages residents to reuse household items.
water supply|The system or quantity of water available for use.|The growing town needs a reliable water supply.
drought|A long period with unusually little rain.|The drought has led to restrictions on garden watering.
flood|Water covering land that is normally dry.|The flood damaged several homes near the river.
erosion|The gradual wearing away of soil or land.|Planting trees can help reduce erosion near the riverbank.
soil|The upper layer of earth in which plants grow.|The garden project tests the soil before planting vegetables.
agriculture|The activity of growing crops and raising animals.|The region depends on agriculture and tourism.
crop|Plants grown for food or another useful purpose.|The dry summer reduced the vegetable crop.
harvest|The collection of crops when they are ready.|Volunteers help with the community orchard harvest.
organic|Produced using methods that restrict certain artificial chemicals.|The market has a stall selling organic vegetables.
local produce|Food grown or made near where it is sold.|The café uses local produce whenever possible.
habitat|The natural place where an organism lives.|The development must protect the birds' nesting habitat.
wildlife|Animals and plants living without being domesticated.|Keep dogs on leads to avoid disturbing wildlife.
urban|Related to a town or city.|Urban residents may have limited access to private gardens.
rural|Related to the countryside rather than towns.|Rural communities need reliable access to health services.
population|The people living in a particular area.|The town's population has grown over the past decade.
migration|Movement of people from one place to live in another.|The article examines migration from rural areas to cities.
isolation|A lack of contact or connection with other people.|The visiting service helps reduce social isolation.
poverty|A lack of money or resources for basic needs.|The charity supports households experiencing poverty.
unemployment|The situation of being without paid work while seeking it.|Local unemployment increased after the factory closed.
opportunity|A chance to do something useful or beneficial.|The new training centre creates an opportunity to learn practical skills.
development|Growth, improvement or the building of something new.|Residents were asked about the proposed housing development.
investment|Money or resources put into something for future benefit.|The town needs investment in reliable public transport.
economy|The system of producing, buying and selling goods and services.|Small businesses play an important role in the local economy.
industry|Businesses involved in a particular type of production or service.|The tourism industry provides many seasonal jobs.
business|An organisation that supplies goods or services.|The new business will employ local residents.
enterprise|An organisation or project, especially one involving initiative.|The community enterprise repairs and sells donated bicycles.
innovation|A useful new idea, method or product.|The award recognises innovation in accessible transport.
technology|Practical use of knowledge to create tools and systems.|New technology allows residents to book appointments online.
digital|Using electronic systems to store or communicate information.|The library provides help with digital applications.
internet access|The ability to connect to online services.|Reliable internet access is important for distance learning.
privacy|Freedom from unwanted access to personal information or activities.|The online service explains how it protects your privacy.
data protection|Rules and practices for safeguarding personal information.|Staff receive training on data protection.
remote working|Doing a job away from the employer's usual premises.|Remote working can reduce the time spent commuting.
flexibility|The ability to adapt to different needs or conditions.|Flexible scheduling offers greater flexibility to working parents.
social change|A change in the way people live and interact in a community.|The growth of remote working has brought social change to the town.
trend|A general direction in which something is changing.|The survey shows a trend towards more online shopping.
evidence|Information that supports a conclusion.|The council asked for evidence of local demand.
statistic|A number describing a group or situation.|Use a relevant statistic to support your argument.
proportion|A part of a total amount or group.|A large proportion of residents travel by bus.
percentage|An amount expressed as parts out of one hundred.|The percentage of households recycling has increased.
increase|To become or make something greater.|The new timetable will increase the number of evening services.
decrease|To become or make something smaller.|The repair programme should decrease water loss.
growth|An increase in size, amount or activity.|Population growth has increased demand for schools.
impact|An important effect on a person or situation.|The report examines the impact of the road closure.
consequence|A result of an action or situation.|Longer journeys are one consequence of the bridge closure.
cause|Something that produces a result or problem.|The survey identified the main cause of delayed deliveries.
factor|Something that influences a result.|Cost is an important factor when choosing a training course.
advantage|A feature that makes something useful or desirable.|One advantage of the new route is its shorter journey time.
disadvantage|A feature that makes something less useful or desirable.|A disadvantage of the venue is the lack of parking.
drawback|A problem or limitation associated with an option.|The main drawback is that the service stops early.
solution|A way to deal successfully with a problem.|The council is looking for a practical solution to congestion.
approach|A way of dealing with a task or problem.|The centre uses a supportive approach to adult learning.
strategy|A planned way of achieving a long-term goal.|The strategy aims to improve access to affordable housing.
measure|An action taken to achieve a particular result.|Better lighting is one measure intended to improve safety.
evaluate|To judge the usefulness or quality of something.|The centre will evaluate the pilot course before expanding it.
monitor|To observe something regularly to check progress or conditions.|Staff monitor water use throughout the summer.
improve|To make or become better.|The changes should improve access to evening classes.
enhance|To make something better or more effective.|The new facilities will enhance the visitor experience.
support|To help something succeed or continue.|The programme will support people returning to work.
promote|To encourage the development or use of something.|The campaign aims to promote cycling to work.
encourage|To help someone feel willing or confident to act.|Discounted fares may encourage more people to use buses.
prevent|To stop something from happening.|Regular maintenance can prevent expensive repairs.
maintain|To keep something in a suitable condition or state.|Volunteers help maintain the community garden.
long-term|Continuing over or relating to an extended period.|The project should bring long-term benefits to residents.
short-term|Continuing over or relating to a limited period.|The closure may cause short-term inconvenience.
effective|Producing the intended result.|The new reminder system is effective in reducing missed appointments.
account for|To explain something or include it in a calculation.|The estimate must account for travel and material costs.
sustainability|Using resources in ways that can continue into the future.|The report considers the sustainability of the proposed development.
resource depletion|The reduction of available natural materials through use.|The article discusses ways to slow resource depletion.
food security|Reliable access to enough suitable food.|Community gardens can contribute to local food security.
biodiversity|The variety of living things in an area.|The planting scheme aims to improve biodiversity.
ecosystem|Living things and their environment interacting as a system.|The wetland is an important part of the local ecosystem.
urbanisation|The growth of towns and cities.|Rapid urbanisation can put pressure on public transport.
integration|The process of becoming part of a wider community.|Language classes can support the integration of new residents.
inequality|An unequal distribution of opportunities or resources.|The report considers inequality in access to education.
infrastructure|Basic systems such as roads, water and communications.|New housing requires investment in local infrastructure.
entrepreneur|Someone who starts and runs a business.|The college offers advice to a first-time entrepreneur.
automation|Using machines or software to perform tasks with less human input.|Automation has changed the skills required in the warehouse.
cybersecurity|Protection of electronic systems and information from attacks.|The small-business workshop includes basic cybersecurity.
adaptation|A change made to suit new conditions.|The building needs adaptation to improve wheelchair access.
implement|To put a plan or decision into practice.|The council will implement the new collection schedule in June.
allocate|To set aside resources for a particular purpose.|The council will allocate funds to accessible playground equipment.
prioritise|To decide that something should receive attention first.|The plan will prioritise repairs near schools.
balance competing needs|To consider different needs when making a decision.|The council must balance competing needs when setting the budget.
feasible|Possible to carry out with the resources available.|The council is checking whether the proposed route is feasible.
equitable|Fair in the way people are treated or resources are shared.|The funding system should provide equitable access to training.
resilience|The ability to recover or adapt after difficulties.|The flood plan aims to strengthen community resilience.
